Posted December 6, 2002
Analysis by Richard Cowan

The December 6, 1972, issue of National Review shocked almost everyone with a cover article calling on Conservatives to support the legalization of marijuana. I wrote that article the first thing that I had ever written for publication with the purpose of convincing Conservatives that they had been deceived by what most government agencies have been telling us for the last forty years.

Now, 30 years later, I want to be more explicit. Although this website is called MarijuanaNews, most of it is not really about cannabis, per se. It is about lying about cannabis, and that was essentially the case with the NR article 30 years ago.

And someone is lying, deliberately trying to deceive the people of the Western democracies. It is my argument the police agencies of DEAland, most other countries, and especially the United Nations, are deliberately lying about their own official data.
See
 Swiss Government Says Going Dutch Does NOT Violate Treaties. Implications for Other Countries, Especially Canada and UK. Plus Full Text of UN Nark Press Release.
and links

Alternatively, you may choose to believe that supporters of medical marijuana and their allies in the broader marijuana reform movement are lying, as John Walters asserts. It must be one or the other. Someoneis lying.

Now consider four key points of the prohibitionist position:

1. Drug Czar John Walters says that " The claim that medical marijuana is an efficacious medicine is a lie. It is used by people who want to legalize marijuana, cynically. " -- Quoted in Canada's Globe and Mail, September 13, 2002

A few days earlier, Richard Meyer, the Drug Enforcement Administration spokesperson in San Francisco, had said, " There is no medical association or scientific organization that has come out to say that marijuana is a medication.

In fact, there are dozens of state and national medical associations from Florida to Finland that have called for medical access to marijuana. Support is particularly strong in groups working with AIDS. Are they risking the lives of their patients in order to legalize marijuana, cynically?
See
 Health Organizations Supporting Immediate Legal Access to Medical Marijuana
and
 Finnish Medical Association Supports Medical Marijuana
And Says Its Negative Effects Have Been Greatly Exaggerated.

Was the Institute of Medicine being cynical when its report sponsored by Walters predecessor, Barry McCaffrey said that " There is no clear alternative for people suffering from chronic conditions that might be relieved by smoking marijuana, such as pain or AIDS wasting " ?

Was the Science and Technology Sub-committee of the House of Lords being cynical in 1998 when it said that " The government should allow doctors to prescribe cannabis for medical use. ... Cannabis can be effective in some patients to relieve symptoms of multiple sclerosis, and against certain forms of pain. ... This evidence is enough to justify a change in the law " ?
See
 Chairman of the House of Lords Science and Technology Committee
Criticizes UK Government's Rejection Of Report On Medical Marijuana
 2 Articles With 2 of the Worst Prohibitionist Arguments
and links

What about the editor of the New England Journal of Medicine? In 1997, he wrote, " Federal authorities should rescind their prohibition of the medical use of marijuana for seriously ill patients and allow physicians to decide which patients to treat

Thousands of patients with cancer, AIDS, and other diseases report they have obtained striking relief from these devastating symptoms by smoking marijuana.
See
 New York Times Runs Pro-Medical Marijuana Op-ed
By National Review Senior Editor Richard Brookhiser

The alleviation of distress can be so striking that some patients and their families have been willing to risk a jail term to obtain or grow the marijuana. "

And that is exactly what is happening.

After DEA agents raided a California cooperative hospice/farm in September to cut down plants its members had grown for their own use, DEA spokesman Meyer said, " we see them as victims of their traffickers. "

Suzanne Pheil, a partially paralyzed post-polio patient who was handcuffed in her bed by the DEA, claims, " We are not the victims of drug traffickers - we are victims of the DEA. With a gun to my head the DEA stole the medicine that over 250 sick and dying people worked to grow. "

Is she lying or is he?

2. Marijuana is so dangerous that its use causes more emergency room visits than heroin. In September, the new Surgeon General, Dr. Richard Carmona, said, Marijuana use as a cause for emergency room visits has risen 176 percent since 1994, surpassing heroin.

First, it should be noted that the Surgeon General is not technically a part of the police apparatus, but in reality everyone in government is a part of the Drug War.

The truth is that the numbers cited Carmona have nothing to do with the cause of emergency room visits.

The numbers represent drug mentions by patients. Emergency room visitors are asked about all of the drugs that they have used. Up to five drugs may be mentioned on the appropriate reporting form. Thus, when heroin addicts go to a hospital seeking treatment for problems with heroin and they report that they have also used marijuana, it will be noted, even though it has nothing to do with the cause of the visit.

In fact, there were only 110,512 mentions of marijuana for 2001, and 75% of those involved mentions of other drugs. This means that there were only about 25,000 marijuana-only mentions out of the 638,484 " drug-related hospital emergency department visits. " This was just one quarter of one tenth of one percent of a total of almost one hundred million ER visits!
See
 Cannabis Prohibition Prostitutes Science In New Emergency Dept. Data. Hiding the Truth Behind A Cloud of Lies.

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, between 20 percent and 30 percent of patients who show up in emergency rooms have alcohol problems. That would be roughly 25 million visits caused by alcohol. Alcohol would appear to cause at least twenty five times and probably one hundred times as many emergency room visits per user as marijuana. And that says nothing about the qualitative differences in the related problems. Does that sound like an unacceptably dangerous drug?

3. Similarly, John Walters claims that " Marijuana is the single biggest drug of addiction in history. " Dr Carmona claims that There are more young people in treatment for marijuana dependency than for alcohol and for all other illegal drugs combined.

The truth is there are roughly 10 million problem drinkers in DEAland, and roughly 40 million daily tobacco smokers, 70% of whom say they want to quit. On the other hand, according to the government's own data, there are only 2 million daily marijuana smokers.

And more than half of the young people who are in treatment for marijuana are there by court order after being arrested. This treatment is a part of programs that are aimed at diverting the kids from the criminal justice system. Many others have been sent by their schools, after being caught holding on the school grounds.
See
 If the Las Vegas Review Journal " Gets It, " Why Don't The Other Papers?

Young kids shouldn't be using marijuana, and I have no difficulty believing that some of them have problems with it, but, under the law, all marijuana use is abuse, so no diagnosis of dependence is necessary for them to be sent for treatment.

Moreover, 90% of the treatment programs are really just classes in which the patients are forced to parrot the party line in order get their records expunged.

Of course, as with the emergency room data, these numbers are used to justify arresting more marijuana users who will be sent for treatment thereby justifying more arrests, and so it goes.

4. There is no alternative to prohibition. The Dutch experience with tolerating cannabis sales and possession has been a disaster, to use Barry McCaffrey's term. In 1998 he claimed that, " The murder rate in Holland is double that in the United States. And the reason is drugs. He also claimed that 9.1 percent teen-agers in the United States report having used cannabis versus 30.2 percent in the Netherlands.
See
 Drug Czar Uses Foreign Affairs Magazine Article For Anti-Dutch Propaganda,
Elevating The Lying To Official Status. Analysis By Richard Cowan

In July of this year an editorial in the Wall Street Journal claimed that there had been vast increases in heroin addiction in Holland as a result of their policies.
See
 My Thanks to the Editors of The Wall Street Journal For Lying to Their Readers (Again) -- Giving Me The Opportunity To Explain Dutch Cannabis Policies (Again).

The truth is that the Dutch murder rate is roughly one-fourth the DEAland rate, and actual numbers for the Dutch last-month-use rate for all Netherlanders between the age of 15 and 34 was just 9.8%, less than one third of the rate McCaffrey claimed.

Moreover, McCaffrey's claim about US teen use did not match any available official US numbers. In fact, the data for 1997, the last year for which McCaffrey would have had the numbers, showed that the last-month-use rate was over 10% -- just among eighth graders! Among American twelfth graders, it was 23.7% -- more than twice that of the Dutch group that included 15 to 34 year-olds.

As for heroin addiction, there are more than twice as many heroin addicts per capita in DEAland than in Holland. In DEAland, the 1999 Monitoring the Future survey found that 2.3% of 8th and 10th graders have used heroin at least once twice the Dutch lifetime prevalence for that group.

See
 The Spin Is Beginning To Wobble On The " Latest Teen Drug Use " Survey. Czar Is " Greatly Encouraged " By Poll Showing Heroin Use By 12th Graders At All Time High.

Now why would the law enforcement agencies of DEAland and the major democracies lie about marijuana, and even about the Netherlands?

Well, in 1972 there were 292,000 marijuana arrests in DEAland. Last year there were over 700,000. Incredibly, there have been more than 14 million marijuana arrests in DEAland since 1972.

These lies, and I have simply chosen a few that are both important and easy to refute, are a part of an ideology that has corrupted law enforcement at every level in DEAland and in most other countries. The DEAland marijuana policy is the use of state violence, even against paralysed women, to maintain prohibition at all costs.

So, if they have lied about something as simple as the support for medical marijuana, or data on emergency room visits, or treatment, or the Dutch experience, then is it not reasonable to be urgently concerned that such people are controlling the police apparatus of the one Superpower? Or are we to think that they have told the truth about everything else?

Sadly, the media and the political establishment not only accept everything that they are told by the police apparatus as true, they even accept the police as experts in many other fields unrelated to their presumed areas of competence.
See
 Negligent Journalism: Reader Beware or A Right to Expect More? The Drug Czar Says He Is Subject to the Scrutiny of the Press. The Significance of the Ultimate Lies. Analysis by Richard Cowan

Narcs with only a high school education are regularly quoted as authorities on child psychology, psychopharmacology, botany, medicine, international law, Dutch social policies, economics, and above all else, the motives of those who criticize them.

Ironically, they often are not even honest or well-informed on law enforcement basics.
See
 Giuliani's Police State Like the Marijuana Prohibition That He Loves Is A Counterproductive Fraud. 3 Articles.
and
 The DEAland Crime Rate May Be Three Times Higher Than Is Reported
and
 Even The Prohibitionists Are Attacking DARE. What Is the Definition of Fraud? Analysis By Richard Cowan

After 30 years, I am all the more convinced that until we address the problem of official lying to justify state violence against cannabis users, we will continue to lose our freedom, and our ability to function as a democratic society.

As Alexander Solzhenitsyn said, Violence can only be concealed by a lie, and the lie can only be maintained by violence. Any man who has once proclaimed violence as his method is inevitably forced to take the lie as his principle.

In short, we really don't have a drug problem. We have a police problem, because the police have a problem with the truth.
See
 The Theory and Practice of Chaos Analysis By Richard Cowan
